quotes.how: parsed with the same routine scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs uses, extracted into this file and run over the resolved intent, so every criterionText is the intent's own text: the 4 criteria it declares are ["SC1","SC2","SC3","SC4"] and scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs compares them character for character
quotes.edges: read from .project/intent/INTENT.md's own five-column edge-coverage table (Edge | Criterion | Category | Disposition | Detail) for the edge-to-criterion rows, and the test-to-edge mapping from .project/plan/PLAN.md's ## Held-out checks section, which this path reads as 8 row(s) of edge -> task -> test in either form a plan writes it - the three-column Edge | Task | Test table, or the bullet '- E.. -> T.. -> test' - so a row cites the suite the milestone's own plan assigns its edges rather than one this file chose: 8 edge row(s) over the criteria ["SC1","SC2","SC3","SC4"] and the suites ["scripts/locale-correctness.test.mjs","scripts/locale-correctness-shapes.test.mjs","scripts/panel-routes.test.mjs"]

why: No row is required, and the list therefore names no driver, no instance and no verdict path: scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs refuses a list with no required row that names a driver, so naming one would be the opposite defect.

The reason is not convenience. A required row must name the driver a control-ai-browsers run expression takes to the wave gate, and that driver must return the gate's four readings - toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext - with the required rows together citing drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext. Every fact the 4 criteria this milestone declares is written about is a reading of this repository's own gate: 8 edge row(s) held by ["scripts/locale-correctness.test.mjs","scripts/locale-correctness-shapes.test.mjs","scripts/panel-routes.test.mjs"], against 12 stage(s) of the check chain. None of them is an element's rect or a dev context, so naming a driver would make the gate return a page reading for a claim about the gate.

The portal is not lost by that ruling: each reason names the clause that would have made a row required, and each row cites the suite the milestone itself assigned its criterion, the reading that suite carries and the commands that prove it.

capture.reading: an armed run re-derives the list from the intent this checkout binds, the five-column edge coverage that intent declares and the suites the plan assigns each criterion, and writes it only when a value moved; a default run reads the file and asserts it is exactly what this head derives.

claims.criterionText: A fixture route that provides a non-default `LOCALE_ID` produces a finding naming the provider entry that carries the token, its kind and its import path, and reports the value as `locale-value-not-recorded`; a mutant that matches the entry by position rather than by token reddens the suite by name. entry that carries it and the formatter the record names; a mutant that restores the default locale turns the finding off and reddens the suite by name.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause makes a verdict required where an insurance-portal route can produce a criterion's facts. SC1 is "A fixture route that provides a non-default `LOCALE_ID` produces a finding naming the provider entry that carries the token, its kind and its import path, and reports the value as `locale-value-not-recorded`; a mutant that matches the entry by position rather than by token reddens the suite by name. entry that carries it and the formatter the record names; a mutant that restores the default locale turns the finding off and reddens the suite by name." - a fact about this repository's own gate, its recordings and the tests that hold them, which no route of any page produces. The portal is named because the clause is answered rather than dodged: the evidence is the edge row(s) ["E1","E2","E7"] the intent itself assigns the criterion, held by ["scripts/locale-correctness.test.mjs","scripts/locale-correctness.test.mjs","scripts/locale-correctness.test.mjs"] and recorded as ["criterion SC1"].
